clue.text: Quarantine flag displayed by jaundiced sailor

parts.note: jaundice turns the skin yellow, so jaundiced means yellow
Jack (Jack Tar) is an old name for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sickly-looking seaman runs up the signal that a ship is in quarantine.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow jack is the plain yellow signal flag a ship flies to show it is under quarantine.

clue.text: The CID in court

definitions.meaning: the Criminal Investigation Department of the Metropolitan Police is based at Scotland ..., often called simply 'the ...'
a courtyard, an enclosed open space beside a building

explanation.definitionFit: London's detectives are known by the name of their headquarters, Scotland Yard; separately, an enclosed courtyard is also called this.

clue.text: Worn-out girl about to be given extreme unction

indicators.note: the girl's word goes around, about, the word for worn-out

parts.note: a lass is a girl
an idea that is worn-out is trite, stale from overuse

explanation.surface: A tired young woman is about to receive the final sacrament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TRITE inside LASS, splitting it after LAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme unction is the Catholic anointing of the dying, part of the sacraments given at the end of life.

clue.text: Had acknowledged the truth

explanation.definitionFit: Possessed something, or admitted a fact: both are senses of the past tense of this verb.

clue.text: A patient man gets numerous odds and ends

parts.note: Job, the Old Testament figure proverbial for patience
lots means many, numerous

explanation.surface: A long-suffering fellow acquires a heap of miscellaneous items.
explanation.definitionFit: Job lots are mixed assortments of goods sold together, so a collection of oddments.

clue.text: Cowherd concocted a fish-soup

indicators.note: concocted means made up or cooked up, so the letters of the cattleman's word are mixed

explanation.surface: A farmhand who tends cattle cooks up a seafood stew.
explanation.definitionFit: Chowder is a thick creamy soup, typically of clams or other fish.

clue.text: Artist with popular backing is an Indian princess

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, a crossword stand-by for an artist

indicators.note: backing tells us the word for popular is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: A painter enjoying public support turns out to be a royal lady from India.
explanation.definitionFit: A rani is the wife or widow of a rajah, or a queen or princess ruling in her own right in India.

clue.text: Saw in the Christian era

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks dates in the Christian reckoning
an age is an era

explanation.surface: A tool or proverb found in the period after Christ.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw in this sense is an old saying or proverb, a maxim.

clue.text: Extreme cruelty inherent in all people

parts.note: inherent in means within, so the word in is supplied
humanity means the whole human race

explanation.surface: Savagery is part of every human being's nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhumanity is a lack of compassion, brutal or savage treatment.

clue.text: Butler put in a small contribution. Isn't that lovely?

indicators.note: put in tells us the politician's name is placed within the word for a share

parts.note: a dole is a small portion or share handed out
Rab Butler, the British Conservative statesman of the mid-20th century

explanation.surface: A butler adds a little donation and admires it.
explanation.walkthrough: RAB is the nickname of the politician R. A. Butler; 'put in' places RAB inside DOLE after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means delightful and charming, worthy of being adored.

clue.text: About to fall from grace, by gum

parts.note: re means concerning, about
to sin is to fall from grace in religious terms

explanation.surface: Someone is on the verge of moral lapse, exclaiming 'by gum'.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is a sticky gum exuded by trees such as pines.

clue.text: What Charlotte Corday did was sheer butchery

definitions.meaning: Corday stabbed the revolutionary Marat while he sat in his bath, filling it with blood

explanation.definitionFit: A massacre is called this; literally it describes Marat's bathtub after his assassin struck.

clue.text: Nail a US president in Yorkshire

parts.note: a brad is a thin flat nail with a small head
Gerald Ford was the 38th President of the United States

explanation.surface: Pinning down an American leader somewhere in northern England.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is indirect: Bradford is a city in West Yorkshire, so 'in Yorkshire' points to a place found there.
explanation.definitionFit: Bradford is a large city in the county of Yorkshire in northern England.

clue.text: Discharge man into a strange environment

indicators.note: into tells us the man's word goes inside the word for odd, its environment

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd, strange
he, the male pronoun, stands for a man

explanation.surface: Releasing a fellow into unfamiliar surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery discharge from the eyes or nose.

clue.text: Tender fish I taken board

parts.note: char is a fish of the trout family
a table, as in board and lodging, food at table

explanation.surface: A gentle fish is brought on board.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'taken' is a link; the fish CHAR, then I, then TABLE for board, run straight on.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable means kindly and generous, tender towards others.

clue.text: The lass crashed, but not in top gear

indicators.note: crashed suggests a smash, so the letters of the phrase are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl had a car accident, though not in the highest gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top gear' means headgear, not a car's fifth gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatless means wearing nothing on the head, the top of the body.

clue.text: Sending out a delegation to Egypt

parts.note: ET is Egypt's code, but E here is taken from the first letter
a mission is a group sent abroad as a delegation

explanation.surface: Dispatching a diplomatic party to Cairo.
explanation.definitionFit: Emission is the act of sending out or giving off something.

clue.text: Fray the feathers, and get given a towelling

parts.note: to fray is to wear by rubbing
down is soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: Ruffling plumage before being dried with a towel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubdown is a brisk rubbing of the body, as with a towel after bathing.

clue.text: So charter is renegotiated by the players

indicators.note: renegotiated means re-worked, so the letters of the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A founding document is redrafted by the participants.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a body of musicians, those who play instruments together.

clue.text: Clairvoyance in a religious ceremony brings relief

indicators.note: in tells us the psychic letters sit inside the ceremony word

parts.note: a rite is a religious ceremony
ESP, extrasensory perception, covers clairvoyance

explanation.surface: A psychic experience during worship offers comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short period of rest or relief from difficulty.

clue.text: Pressing a fellow to join the English cricket team

parts.note: a cricket side has eleven players, written XI in Roman numerals
a gent is a gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: Urging a chap to join the national cricket side.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are given out of answer order: E and XI come before GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means urgent, demanding immediate attention.

clue.text: Fellows who've got it never turn a hair

definitions.text: Fellows who've got it never turn a hair

parts.words: Fellows who've got it never turn a hair
parts.note: a man with this very short haircut has no hair long enough to turn or ruffle

explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is a very short, bristly haircut, worn traditionally by men.

clue.text: Miscreant priest-one in an ex-exclusive sect

indicators.note: in tells us the priest and one go inside the sect word

parts.note: a cult is a small, exclusive religious sect
I, the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wrongdoing cleric belongs to a closed religious group.
explanation.definitionFit: A culprit is a person responsible for a wrong, a miscreant.

clue.text: In a setback I'd experience ups and downs

indicators.note: in tells us ID sits within the turned word
back tells us the word is turned round

parts.note: set is taken as written
I'd gives ID

explanation.surface: After a reversal of fortune, I'd go through highs and lows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SET into TES, and 'In' puts ID inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tides rise and fall each day, so ups and downs of the sea.

clue.text: He's a fool to press the Anglican church for money

parts.note: to dun is to press a debtor for payment
CE, the Church of England

explanation.surface: Anyone who demands cash from the Church is an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for money' only completes the sense of 'press' as dun, a demand for payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is a slow-witted person, a fool.

clue.text: Sick and overweight, Edward is mostunfortunate

parts.note: ill means sick
fat means overweight
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: An ailing, heavy man named Edward is very unlucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-fated means doomed, destined for misfortune.

clue.text: Opposed to constant buffoonery

parts.note: anti means opposed to, against
c is the symbol for a constant, notably the speed of light

explanation.surface: Being against endless clowning around.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a grotesque or absurd act, clownish behaviour.

clue.text: Run quickly and hide

definitions.meaning: an animal's skin with the fur still on

explanation.definitionFit: Rushing headlong is one sense; an animal skin with fur is the other.

clue.text: Musicians love to ogle a cartridge-case

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
to leer is to ogle, look at lustfully

explanation.surface: Players love eyeing a bullet holder.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandoleer is a shoulder belt with loops or pockets to hold cartridges.

clue.text: Turn it over to the church!

definitions.text: Turn it over to the church!

indicators.note: over tells us the little word is flipped to read backwards

parts.note: it is taken as written
the is taken as written

explanation.surface: An exhortation to hand one's money over to the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns IT into TI, then THE follows; the whole clue also describes paying the levy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe is a tenth of produce or income given to the church.

clue.text: Perpetually heartless evil-doer

indicators.note: heartless means the central letters are removed from the word

parts.note: evil-doer is taken as written

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer forever lacking compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' strips the middle letters ILDO, leaving the outer letters EV and ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means always, at all times.

clue.text: Government trade census?

parts.note: read as a survey of national craftsmen, it points to the art of running a country

explanation.definitionFit: Statecraft is the skill of governing, the business of running a nation.
